newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Iskra cuts H1 loss, aims for breakeven.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Iskra cuts H1 loss, aims for breakeven.

text.p: Slovenian electronic appliance producer Iskra Holding said on Tuesday it managed to reduce its first half pre-tax loss and boost turnover, putting it on course to break even for the full year.

The company's first half pre-tax loss fell to 324 million tolars ($2.3 million) from about 600 million in the same period of 1995. Sales rose to 24.6 billion tolars from 24.3 billion in the same period of 1995.
"Our main plans to the end of the year are to get out of the red and complete our privatisation process," general manager Dusan Sesok told Reuters.
The company said it expected sales at the end of the year to reach 56.7 billion tolars.
"These expectations are realistic based on the usual dynamics of our business. Generally most of our sales are made in the second half of the year," Sesok said.
Iskra traced the rise in sales to strong exports, which accounted for 60 percent of sales in the first half of the year, up from 54 percent in the same period of 1995.
